newsitem.title: GERMANY: ROWING-GERMANY SPARKLE AT NEW WORLD CUP.
newsitem.headline: ROWING-GERMANY SPARKLE AT NEW WORLD CUP.

text.p: Germany again stole the show by qualifying 16 crews for the finals of the first regatta on the second day of the new rowing World Cup on Saturday.
Next best were Denmark, France and Britain, each with four boats qualifying for Sunday's finals.
Lithuania, the Netherlands, Poland and Russia won three finals places apiece as strong head winds made racing conditions difficult and times slow for the second successive day.

Many of the German crews are new this season but among the big names who reached the finals were Olympic and world medallists Stephen Volkert and Andreas Hajek in the men's double sculls and Andre Willms in the men's single sculls.
There will be two German crews in the finals of six events.

Highlights of the day's racing included a surprise win in the second semifinal of the men's single sculls by Ibrahim Ali of Egypt ahead of the favourite, double Olympic quadruple sculls champion Willms.
An unexpected finalist was American Jamie Koven, unknown as a sculler but a member of the U.S. eight who won gold at the 1994 world championships.
The new British coxless four, with Olympic stars Steve Redgrave and Matthew Pinsent, produced another impressive performance to win their semifinal by over a length, easing down.
Coach Jurgen Grobler warned afterwards: "There's much more to come. I can see a lot of power there."
